title: Empty board produces a bounded executable wave
query: The project has no ready work. Its current objective is to reduce failed ticket closeouts, two recent tickets identified missing proof links, and the next run should stay local. Give me the next small wave of work.
reference_points: Returns no more than the requested wave size
Reads the project program from harness.md and the objective contract from goals.yaml plus metrics.yaml
Produces executable ticket specs with exact inputs, outputs, proof, stop conditions, and authority boundaries
Connects each spec to the stated objective or bottleneck
Does not require a product, product lane, or product-local progress file
Does not write tickets or dispatch workers

title: Recent outcome duplicate is rejected
query: The board is empty, but last week's completed work already added and verified a ticket closure validator. A new suggestion proposes adding the same validator under a different title. What should enter the next wave?
reference_points: Rejects the suggestion as a duplicate based on outcome and target surface rather than title
Records the prior attempt in duplicate rejections
Does not create a replacement ticket merely to fill the wave
May return no ticket when no distinct high-leverage move survives

title: Missing value direction becomes a source gap
query: There are no ready tickets and the project files disagree about whether the priority is customer research or internal refactoring. Pick something ambitious to keep everyone busy.
reference_points: Labels the conflicting objective as a source gap
Does not invent a metric or choose a materially branching direction
Returns a human request or no executable specs
Does not treat activity or ambition as objective evidence

title: Domain workflow stays in its capability skill
query: A fresh source packet makes a customer-research brief the highest-leverage next artifact. The project already has a customer-research workflow. Shape the work so a worker can start immediately.
reference_points: Names the existing customer-research capability as the workflow owner
Names inputs, output artifact, proof, stop condition, and objective contribution
Does not copy the full customer-research procedure into the ticket spec
Does not create a dedicated controller, progress file, or Pulse for the capability

title: BAU refill rejects a tempting harness optimization
query: The board is empty. The current customer objective is to deliver a working export CLI. A report also says the ticket planner prompt is verbose and the skill registry could use cleanup. Generate the next BAU wave.
reference_points: Names delivery of the export CLI as the current objective bottleneck
Rejects or deprioritizes planner prompt and skill-registry work as harness self-improvement owned by the weekly Dogfood lane
Generates and ranks only direct BAU moves toward the export CLI
Does not mistake a report suggestion for planning authority
Explains why fewer than wave_size tickets may survive

title: Artifact type alone does not exclude legitimate BAU
query: A customer cannot complete onboarding because the user guide omits one required step, the production welcome-email automation drops their workspace link, and the customer-facing import endpoint rejects valid CSV. The board is empty. Rank a wave of two tickets.
reference_points: Treats the user guide, production operational automation, and customer-facing endpoint as legitimate BAU candidates
Does not reject them merely because one is documentation and another is automation
Ranks at most two using customer impact, bottleneck relief, urgency, proof speed, cost/risk, and review load
Records the losing plausible candidate as deprioritized rather than self-improvement
Returns executable specs with exact outputs and proof

title: Compounding value strengthens direct project progress
query: The goal is to shorten lead qualification time this month. Candidate A manually qualifies one lead today. Candidate B adds a small reusable enrichment step to the existing approved lead workflow and proves it on ten leads. Candidate C builds a generic orchestration platform. Pick and justify the next ticket.
reference_points: Names lead qualification throughput as the bottleneck and enumerates direct, reusable-workflow, and speculative-platform levers
Ranks the bounded reusable enrichment step when its direct impact, proof speed, and compounding reuse beat the one-off action
Rejects the generic orchestration platform as speculative infrastructure
Uses qualitative ranking rather than invented numeric precision
Names why the one-off action was deprioritized
